mnemora.boundary: Hard-fails on any non-public repository; private aggregates are a separate, auth-gated workflow.
mnemora.purpose: Collect EVERY public repository of the configured owners into the normalized cache. Discovery is scoped to the public repository listing, so private repositories cannot enter this path.

nodes.name: Manual Run
nodes.notes:
START HERE TO RUN IT BY HAND.

This node does nothing automatically. It exists so a person (or the scripts/workflows.sh helper) can trigger the workflow on demand.

The scheduled start is the other node beside it. You need one of these because the n8n command line refuses to run a workflow whose only start is a schedule.

nodes.name: Every Hour
nodes.notes: Runs hourly: GitHub's rate limit window refreshes hourly, so an hourly pass keeps the database at most an hour behind without ever approaching the quota. An idle run costs one listing call.

nodes.name: Build Plan
nodes.notes:
READS THE SETTINGS BEFORE TOUCHING THE NETWORK.

It decides: which accounts to look at, how much history to fetch, whether forks and archived repositories count, and whether a GitHub token is available.

It sends nothing and fetches nothing. That is the point: a typo in .env fails here in under a second with a clear message, instead of halfway through a two-minute crawl.

The output is one small object describing the whole run.

nodes.name: Collect
nodes.notes: Decides, per repository, whether to fetch. Its input is now the database (Read State), not the cache files: pushed_at_utc from the row answers 'did this move'. Three outcomes: skipped (nothing fetched, record sent with commits_omitted so timestamps advance without deleting rows), full (changed or unknown repository, whole commit history), error (fetch failed, nothing sent that could prune). It also reports repositories that vanished from the listing so the database can archive them.

nodes.name: To JSON File
nodes.notes:
TURNS EACH RECORD INTO A FILE, IN MEMORY.

One file per repository, each containing a single plain JSON object. Nothing is written to disk yet — this step only produces the bytes the next node saves.

nodes.name: Write Public Cache
nodes.notes:
SAVES THE FILES WHERE THE DASHBOARD WILL READ THEM.

The filename is not guessed here: it comes from a field the record already carries (cache_file), so a file can never disagree with its own contents.

In queue mode the WORKER container runs this, which is why the cache volume is mounted on the worker as well as the main instance — otherwise the files would vanish on restart.

nodes.name: Read State
nodes.notes: Replaces the two file-reading nodes. Reads what the database already knows about every repository — pushed_at_utc, commit_count, source_state, whether it was archived — using a read-only role that cannot write. An empty table here is a real cold start, not a missing cache. If this node fails the run stops: guessing 'no state' would re-fetch every repository and burn the API budget.

nodes.name: Acquire Run Lock
nodes.notes: Asks persist for the single-run lease before any GitHub call. If another run holds it, this fails immediately with the holder's id and expiry instead of duplicating a 24-repository crawl. TTL bounds a crashed run. Set COLLECT_010_RUN_LOCK=false to bypass deliberately.

nodes.name: Release Run Lock
nodes.notes: Returns the lease once all fetching and storing is done, so the next run is not blocked for the rest of the TTL. Non-fatal on purpose: a failure here must not fail a run whose data is already stored — the lease expires on its own.

nodes.name: Record Run
nodes.notes: Files the run's own report in mnemora_runs: repositories fetched, skipped, deferred, failed and archived, commits the pipe reported, and API calls spent. Counts come from the status item and from persist's per-record answers — nothing is estimated. Non-fatal: a run that stored data must not fail because its report did.
